purpose: Diagnose the dry linear-reservoir rate law on an author-published column tail; not a whole-site validation or externally blind qualification.

source.processing: Author-supplied drainage rate series; article reports30s aggregation and plateau LOESS. No additional smoothing.

priorExposure: README gives author viscous-flow front estimate64830s and nominal forcing; therefore this is a development diagnosis, not independent model selection.
Only schema/timestamps inspected from exact downloaded data before this freeze.

calibration.q0: Median original rates at0.9*64410 <= time <=64410, prescribed by author before inspecting values
calibration.tail: All19 original rows with0 < time-64410 <=570 seconds

heldChallenge.rows: All19 original rows with570 < time-64410 <=1140 seconds
heldChallenge.mustNotInfluence: q0, coefficient fitting, bounds, family, starts, ranking or training objective

models.fit: k in[0,100]/hour; exact bounded scalar least squares on original training rates. Actual maintained advanceDrainingLayer checked for every candidate evaluation output.
lagSeconds in[0,570] and k in[0,100]/hour; lag integer seconds exhaustively, bounded scalar k. Additional free lag disclosed.
lagSeconds in[0,570], exponent fixed1.5 from primary author model, exact bounded scalar least squares.

metrics: Original rate RMSE in mm/hour for calibration and held separately
Trapezoidal volume over sampled held interval only, explicitly derived and not original cumulative drainage evidence
negativeControls: Replace all held rates by wrong nonnegative rates and require exact same fits; score must change.
All constant-zero calibration must not fabricate informative k or comparative success.
Actual maintained kernel and declared dry exponential law must agree; no substituted kernel.
limits: Only one short processed column course; no measurement half-widths supplied.
Bottom suction,17.9h forcing and missing surface observations exclude whole-event receiving-band admission.
A better tail fit cannot establish physical mechanism, parameter truth, whole-event prediction, or benefits on independently new data.
